title: LLM quality regression alerting and dashboard guidelines
author: Marina Alvarez
content:
Overview

This document defines the standard dashboards, alerting rules, and operational playbook for detecting and responding to LLM quality regressions in the Redwood platform. It is intended to help platform engineers, oncall operators, and SREs detect regressions early (model drift, quantization artifacts, prompt-change regressions, and infra-induced degradation) and run a structured investigation and mitigation.

Goals

- Detect user-visible degradation in model output quality before downstream product metrics (NPS, retention) are impacted.
- Provide reproducible signal definitions and dashboard templates that product and platform teams can reuse.
- Tie alerts to actionable runbooks and clear ownership to reduce mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) and mean-time-to-repair (MTTR).

Scope

This guide covers: hosted and dedicated Redwood API routes and model variants, evaluation harness signal ingestion, dashboard panels, Prometheus/Tempo/Trace query examples, alert severities and thresholds, and the triage + mitigation playbook. It does not replace model-level offline evals (see applied-ml-and-evals) but complements them with production signals.

Key signal categories (what to monitor)

1) Prompt-set regression checks (primary signal)
- Periodically run a canonical prompt-set (golden prompts) against the production model variant and record: response hash, normalized BLEU/ROUGE/EMB similarity, semantic similarity to baseline embedding, and canned evaluation metrics.
- Metric names: llm.eval.promptset.similarity, llm.eval.promptset.score.mean, llm.eval.promptset.delta_from_baseline
- Preferred cadence: every 15m for high-traffic routes, 1h for lower-traffic routes.

2) Semantic embedding drift
- Track mean cosine similarity between recent responses and a rolling baseline embedding for the same prompt set. Large negative shifts indicate drift or changed decoding behavior.
- Metric: llm.response.embedding.cosine_mean (labels: route, model_version, region)

3) Token-level log-probability and perplexity changes
- Sudden changes in average token log-probability or per-response perplexity often correlate with hallucination or low-quality outputs.
- Metrics: llm.token.logprob.mean, llm.response.perplexity.p99

4) Output length and stop-token anomalies
- Monitor changes in mean response length and frequency of missing stop tokens (truncated or runaway generations).
- Metrics: llm.response.length.mean, llm.response.truncated.count

5) User feedback / correctness signals (business-derived)
- Tie explicit user flags (thumbs-down, report) and implicit downstream failure counts (reranks, retries) into early-warning dashboards.
- Ingested metrics: user.feedback.negative.rate, service.retries.per_request

6) Side-channel infra signals (correlated failures)
- GPU memory pressure, KV cache miss-rate spikes, or excessive tail latency can manifest as quality regressions (e.g., shorter outputs). Correlate these to rule out infra causes.
- Metrics: infra.gpu.memory.util, runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate, llm.request.tail_latency_ms.p99

Dashboard templates and recommended panels

Provide these panels as reusable templates in Grafana/Redwood Console. Each panel must include the primary metric, a breakdown by model_version and route, and an annotation stream for deploys and config changes. Required panels:

- Prompt-set similarity heatmap
  - X axis: time, Y axis: prompt id. Color: llm.eval.promptset.similarity.
  - Useful query: average by (prompt_id) (llm.eval.promptset.similarity{route=~"$route", model_version=~"$model"})

- Rolling baseline delta (1h/6h/24h)
  - Line series: llm.eval.promptset.delta_from_baseline (1h), (6h), (24h) to show trend windows.

- Embedding cosine mean by route/model
  - Top N routes with largest negative delta in the last hour.

- Token logprob distribution (histogram)
  - Shows change in distribution shape indicating probability collapse or bursty low-confidence tokens.

- Response perplexity p50/p90/p99
  - Use summary panels showing percentiles and recent percent change.

- Response length and truncation rate
  - Two-axis panel: mean length and truncated.count rate.

- Correlation dashboard: quality signals vs infra signals
  - Shared time window correlation matrix (embedding delta vs gpu memory vs tail latency).

- User feedback overlay and funnel
  - Timeline overlay of user negative feedback events with prompt-set deltas and deploy annotations.

Alerting rules and severities (recommended defaults)

All alerts must include: affected route(s), model_version, timeframe, and suggested next-step (runbook link). Attach a reproducible check job ID when firing.

Severity: P0 (page)
- Trigger WHEN: prompt-set score mean drops by >= 15% from baseline AND absolute llm.eval.promptset.score.mean < 0.6 in a 10-minute window for a customer-facing critical route.
- Rationale: strong signal of major quality degradation.
- Pager: SRE oncall and Product owner.

Severity: P1 (pager + Slack channel)
- Trigger WHEN: embedding cosine_mean drops by >= 8% relative to rolling 24h baseline for >= 30 minutes OR perplexity p99 increases by >= 40% over baseline.
- Pager: Platform oncall, CC product engineering.

Severity: P2 (alerting to ticketing)
- Trigger WHEN: response.truncated.count increases 2x baseline OR mean response length falls by >= 30% for a non-critical route for > 1 hour.

Noise controls and adaptive thresholds

- Use rolling baselines and relative-delta thresholds rather than absolute thresholds for routes with high variance.
- Apply per-route normalization buckets (chat vs summarization vs embedding-only routes) to avoid false positives.
- Implement cooldowns and alert-quorums: require signal to be present in at least two categories (e.g., prompt-set delta + embedding delta) for P1/P0 alerts unless the metric is unambiguous.

Instrumentation and metric collection guidance

- Evaluation harness jobs must attach deterministic metadata: route id, request id, model_version, commit_sha, harness_job_id.
- Sample raw response text is stored in a bounded-length trace (Gzipped) referenced by trace_id in metric labels; do not store PII.
- Export embedding vectors as a decayed aggregate (centroid) to reduce storage. Avoid storing per-request full vectors long-term.

Prometheus / Loki / Tempo examples

PromQL example - prompt-set mean similarity (1h avg):
avg_over_time(llm_eval_promptset_similarity{route="chat/main",model_version=~"v.*"}[1h])

Alert rule YAML (example, simplified):
- alert: PromptSetMeanDropCritical
  expr: (avg_over_time(llm_eval_promptset_score_mean{route=~"$route"}[10m]) < 0.6) and ( (avg_over_time(llm_eval_promptset_score_mean{route=~"$route"}[10m]) / avg_over_time(llm_eval_promptset_score_mean{route=~"$route"}[24h])) < 0.85 )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: P0
  annotations:
    summary: "Prompt-set mean score drop for {{ $labels.route }}"

Investigation runbook (triage checklist)

1) Confirm alert details
- Document alert ID, firing time, affected routes and model_version, and attached harness_job_id.

2) Reproduce with golden prompt-set
- Run the golden prompt set against the currently-serving model_version and the previous stable version. Record response hashes and metric deltas.

3) Correlate infra signals
- Check GPU memory pressure, KV cache hit rate, disk IO, and request tail latencies for the same timeframe.

4) Check recent deployments and config changes
- Look at recent canary rollouts, quantization profile switches, or runtime kernel changes. Use deploy annotations on dashboards.

5) If model variant shows regression, roll back or route to canary-stable path
- For Dedicated/private deployments, consult Private upgrade policy. For hosted routes, use automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants.

6) If infra-correlated, follow infra runbooks (gpu-fleet/gpu-interference or kv-cache repair)

Mitigations matrix (quick actions)

- Model-behavior regressions:
  - Immediate: route to stable model_variant, throttle new requests, increase sampling of golden prompts.
  - Short term: hotfix prompt engineering or decoding parameter adjustments (temperature, top-k/top-p), run constrained decode tests.
  - Long term: model rollback and offline retrospective evaluation.

- Quantization/regeneration artifacts:
  - Immediate: disable quantized fast-path for affected model_version or switch to higher-precision fallback.
  - Short term: re-run quantization with updated calibration set and run the harness.

- Infra-induced quality changes:
  - Immediate: scale capacity or evict noisy tenants, restart affected pods in a controlled fashion.
  - Short term: schedule maintenance window for kernel/driver updates or re-balance cache shards.

Operational playbook for onboarding a new route

1) Create golden prompt-set (30–200 prompts) with product and applied-ml team. Label prompts with expected behaviours and regression sensitivity.
2) Add instrumenting harness job (15m cadence for critical routes).
3) Wire dashboard template to route (copy panels, set $route variable).
4) Configure alerting with conservative thresholds and a 72-hour monitoring period to calibrate baselines.
5) Post calibration, run an analyst review and freeze alert thresholds or move to adaptive-mode.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: Platform Observability team (first responder for triage).
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime team (for model infra and kernel issues).
- Product owner and Model Owner: Required for P0 and P1 incidents.

Escalation path: Platform oncall -> Serving Runtime engineer -> Model owner -> Product owner -> VP Eng if P0 persists > 60m.

Instrumentation checklist for auditors

- All alerts must include a non-PHI sample response trace id.
- Golden prompt sets and evaluations are stored in the evaluations bucket with retention policy of 90 days by default.
- Any exception to retention or extra sampling must be approved by Security and documented.

Post-incident analysis and continuous improvement

- Add a regression test to the eval-harness for any confirmed production regression scenario (include prompt, baseline response, and failing model metadata).
- Tag dashboards and alerts with lessons learned and calibration notes.
- Quarterly review: reconcile platform-detected regressions with offline evals to identify gaps in prompt-sets or metrics.

Appendices

A. Example prompt-set schema
- prompt_id, route, text, expected_keywords, sensitivity_score (1–5), owner

B. Suggested metric labels
- route, model_version, region, tier, commit_sha, harness_job_id

C. Further reading and links
- Applied ML eval-harness (link: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness)
- Runtime k-v cache monitoring (link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/kv-cache-monitoring)

Contact

For questions or onboarding help, contact the Platform Observability team via #platform-observability and use the page's reviewers list for ad-hoc reviews.
